clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-year-old female with known Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) presented to Tabriz Dentistry Hospital with dental caries and tooth pain. She had a documented history of seizures (treated with Carbamazepine and Phenobarbital) and intellectual disability. Physical examination revealed characteristic facial angiofibromas (wart-like lesions) in a butterfly distribution involving the nose, present since age 7 years, with the largest lesion measuring 0.5 cm. Panoramic radiography demonstrated hypoplastic enamel requiring endodontic treatment. Brain MRI and CT performed during her neurological workup revealed multiple cortical and subcortical glioneuronal tubers and subependymal glial nodules, with no evidence of giant cell astrocytomas or aneurysm. Systemic evaluation showed no involvement of heart, kidneys, lungs, bones, or eyes, and laboratory tests were normal.
